claim: Whether neural collapse (the last-layer features and classifier weights settling into a symmetric simplex configuration late in training) emerges depends on how the optimizer applies weight decay: adaptive optimizers that add weight decay to the gradient (Adam, Signum) produce it, while the same optimizers with decoupled weight decay (AdamW, SignumW) do not, even at far larger weight decay. Supported only if, across ResNet9 and VGG9 on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 over a grid of learning rates, momenta and weight decays, the decoupled variants end with higher NC0 (squared row sum of the last-layer weights, which must vanish under collapse) and NC3 than the coupled variants at every weight decay; if in the reference setting AdamW's NC0 ends above its initial value while Adam's falls by at least 80% and AdamW reduces NC3 by under 50% against at least 75% for Adam; if shifting weight decay from the decoupled to the coupled form at fixed total strength lowers NC0 and NC3 steadily without changing validation accuracy; and if Adam versus AdamW on ResNet50 / ImageNet shows the same gap.

experiments: Define the grid and metrics. Setup: ResNet9 and VGG9 on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 with SGD, SGDW, Adam, AdamW, Signum and SignumW; three learning rates, six momenta and six weight decays each (3,888 runs, about 2,500 kept after discarding runs that failed to train), 200 epochs, batch 128, step decay by 10x at one and two thirds. Metrics: NC1 (within-class variability), NC2 (class means and weights form a simplex), NC3 (self-duality of weights and means), and the new NC0 = squared norm of the last-layer weights' row sum, which must reach zero for collapse (necessary, not sufficient); NC4 is dropped because it holds whenever training accuracy nears 100%. Collapse strength is judged relative to initial values and to the best values seen.

Compare coupled and decoupled weight decay. Setup: final metrics across weight decays (averaged over learning rates and momenta) and full trajectories on ResNet9 / FashionMNIST. Result: in the reference run NC0 / NC1 / NC2 / NC3 end at 2.1e-4 / 0.05 / 0.29 / 0.35 for SGD, 0.55 / 0.26 / 0.46 / 0.80 for SGDW, 0.34 / 0.04 / 0.29 / 0.29 for Adam (NC0 -80.6%, NC3 -79.5%), 5.33 / 0.20 / 0.54 / 0.78 for AdamW (NC0 far above initial, NC3 -45.2%), 0.78 / 0.13 / 0.50 / 0.58 for Signum and 3,186 / 0.30 / 1.15 / 1.40 for SignumW. AdamW and SignumW stay above Adam and Signum on NC0 and NC3 even with weight decay orders of magnitude larger; the smallest singular value of the last-layer weights grows under AdamW and SignumW. The pattern repeats on the other architecture-dataset pairs and on ResNet50 / ImageNet (Adam vs AdamW, 90 epochs).

Interpolate between Adam and AdamW. Setup: ResNet9 / MNIST, momentum 0.9, total weight decay fixed at 0.0005 split between a coupled and a decoupled part. Result: moving weight decay into the coupled part steadily lowers NC0, NC2 and NC3 while validation accuracy stays essentially the same, so collapse and generalisation come apart. Theory on sign gradient descent (Adam with beta1 = beta2 = 0) in the unconstrained-feature model: with decoupled decay NC0 rises monotonically to (K-2)^2 / lambda^2; with coupled decay a decaying learning rate exists that drives it to zero; a small MLP experiment shows the predicted non-monotone versus saturating NC0 curves.

Check partial collapse and the limits of the evidence. Setup: the run with the smallest NC3 and over 99% training accuracy per optimizer; preliminary ViT runs on CIFAR-10. Result: in its best run AdamW reaches the lowest NC1 (0.01) and NC2 (0.14) of all optimizers while NC0 is 8.09 and NC3 0.49 (Adam 0.12 / 0.04 / 0.23 / 0.17; SGDW 1.5e-4 / 0.01 / 0.15 / 0.10), so collapse properties do not always appear together and SGDW can collapse fully. In ViTs NC0 first rises then falls for both Adam and AdamW and NC3 is U-shaped, with runs kept at only 50% training accuracy. Theory covers only SGD and sign descent on the unconstrained-feature model, and Table 1's summary marks convergence for the decoupled case and none for the coupled case, the reverse of the theorem statements.
